part: 12 V Feetech ST-3215-C018 serial bus servo
why: No US-made serial-bus servo was found that meets 30 kg.cm at 12 V, 0.222 s/60 deg, 45.2 x 24.7 x 35 mm, the 25T spline, and half-duplex TTL with 4096 counts. ProModeler DS270DLHV is $54.99 and 270 oz-in, which is 19.44 kg.cm (calc only), under 30 kg.cm. The DL series text on that page tops out at 360 oz-in, which is 25.92 kg.cm (calc only). The page does not print a US factory sentence or a serial bus. GearWurx Mini-Torxis is $79.99, 700 oz-in (4.9 N.m on the page) and 0.13 s per 60 deg, and it fails the bus (PWM), the travel (180 deg), and the mass (158 g against 55 g). The page does not print a country of origin. Teknic describes itself as a US manufacturer in Victor, NY, and ClearPath models start at $249. The user manual lists the smallest frame as NEMA 23 with a body length code of 82 mm. That is not this pocket, and the command is step or Teknic software, not the Feetech bus. Glentek says it manufactures in El Segundo, California. The small GMB2005-8 continuous torque on the category page is 0.27 Nm, under 2.942 Nm, and no catalog price was printed. The Feetech page footer prints a Shenzhen address. Not a pass.
twin_followup: Any real swap changes mass, the torque curve, the case, the spline, and the bus. Run C would have to be trained again. Not done here.
